words.gloss: by abandonment of the group of six enemies

hindi: इसलिए छह शत्रुओं के वर्ग के त्याग से इन्द्रिय-जय करे; वृद्धों के सम्पर्क से प्रज्ञा; चर से नेत्र; उद्यम से योग और क्षेम का साधन; कार्य के निर्देश से अपने धर्म की स्थापना; विनय विद्या के उपदेश से; अर्थ के सम्पर्क से लोक-प्रियता; हित से वृत्ति।
english: Therefore [he] should make conquest of the senses through abandonment of the group of six enemies; wisdom through association with elders; the eye through a spy; the means of acquisition and security through exertion; the establishing of own dharma through instruction in tasks; discipline through teaching of learning; dearness to the people through connection with wealth; conduct through the beneficial.
notes: Prose rule. kurvīta governs every object in the series (the verb is not repeated), so the later items are verbless in the translation. The six enemies are not named here. cakṣuḥ = the eye (faculty of seeing), the text does not say more. utthāna = rising up, exertion. kārya-anuśāsana: 'instruction in tasks' is literal; who instructs is not stated. vṛtti could also be 'livelihood'; hita could be taken as 'the beneficial' or 'benefit'. cāra = spy (singular, instrumental). '-' in tyāgena-indriya is the e-text's unsandhied join of two words; samyoga is the e-text's regular spelling of saṃyoga.
lines_deva: तस्माद् अरि.षड्.वर्ग.त्यागेन-इन्द्रिय.जयं कुर्वीत, वृद्ध.सम्योगेन प्रज्ञाम्, चारेण चक्षुः, उत्थानेन योग.क्षेम.साधनम्, कार्य.अनुशासनेन स्वधर्म.स्थापनम्, विनयं विद्या.उपदेशेन, लोक.प्रियत्वम् अर्थ.सम्योगेन, हितेन वृत्तिम्
lines_iast: tasmād ari.ṣaḍ.varga.tyāgena-indriya.jayaṃ kurvīta, vṛddha.samyogena prajñām, cāreṇa cakṣuḥ, utthānena yoga.kṣema.sādhanam, kārya.anuśāsanena svadharma.sthāpanam, vinayaṃ vidyā.upadeśena, loka.priyatvam artha.samyogena, hitena vṛttim

words.gloss: injuries to the women and property of others

hindi: इस प्रकार वश में इन्द्रियों वाला दूसरों की स्त्री और धन की हिंसाओं को और नींद, चंचलता, झूठ, उद्धत-वेशत्व, निरर्थक का सम्पर्क, अधर्म से युक्त और अनर्थ से युक्त व्यवहार को छोड़े।
english: In this way, with controlled senses, [he] should avoid injuries to the women and property of others, and sleep, fickleness, falsehood, haughtiness of dress, connection with the worthless, and dealings connected with unrighteousness and connected with loss.
notes: Prose rule; the subject of varjayet is unstated. The first ca links the injuries with the list that follows; the second ca joins the two participial phrases qualifying vyavahāra. laulya could also be 'greed'; svapna 'sleep' (or dreaming); uddhata = haughty, unruly, so uddhata-veṣatva is literally 'the state of having a haughty dress'. anarthya taken as 'the worthless' (persons or things not stated); anartha = loss, 'harm' is possible. hiṃsā governs both strī and dravya of others (para). Whether para-strī-dravya is a dvandva of strī and dravya under para is a reading choice.
lines_deva: एवं वश्य.इन्द्रियः पर.स्त्री.द्रव्य.हिंसाश् च वर्जयेत्, स्वप्नं लौल्यम् अनृतम् उद्धत.वेषत्वम् अनर्थ्य.सम्योगम् अधर्म.सम्युक्तम् अनर्थ.सम्युक्तं च व्यवहारम्
lines_iast: evaṃ vaśya.indriyaḥ para.strī.dravya.hiṃsāś ca varjayet, svapnaṃ laulyam anṛtam uddhata.veṣatvam anarthya.samyogam adharma.samyuktam anartha.samyuktaṃ ca vyavahāram

words.gloss: by non-opposition to dharma and wealth

hindi: धर्म और अर्थ के अविरोध से काम का सेवन करे, सुख से रहित न हो।
english: [He] should pursue desire without conflict with dharma and wealth, [he] should not be without happiness.
notes: Prose rule; the subject is unstated. nihsukhaḥ is the e-text's habitual h for visarga before a sibilant. seveta: √sev = serve, follow, indulge in; 'pursue' chosen.
lines_deva: धर्म.अर्थ.अविरोधेन कामं सेवेत, न निह्सुखः स्यात्
lines_iast: dharma.artha.avirodhena kāmaṃ seveta, na nihsukhaḥ syāt

hindi: अथवा समान रूप से त्रिवर्ग, परस्पर जुड़ा हुआ।
english: Or [he should pursue] the triad equally, mutually connected.
notes: Elliptical: the verb seveta of the preceding unit is understood and is bracketed in English only. samam may be adverbial ('equally') or an adjective of trivargam ('the equal triad'). The triad is dharma, artha and kāma, as the next unit shows; the text does not name it here. GROUPING: this and the preceding unit form one sentence ('Or ...').

words.gram: past part. pass. m. nom. sg. ati-ā-√sev

hindi: क्योंकि धर्म, अर्थ, काम में से एक, अत्यधिक सेवन किया गया, अपने को और दूसरे दोनों को पीड़ित करता है।
english: For one of dharma, wealth and desire, excessively pursued, afflicts itself and the other two.
notes: The genitive dharma-artha-kāmānām is partitive ('one of'). atyāsevita: ati-ā-√sev; the participle is not given a conditional sense in the translation.
lines_deva: एको ह्य् अत्यासेवितो धर्म.अर्थ.कामानाम् आत्मानम् इतरौ च पीडयति
lines_iast: eko hy atyāsevito dharma.artha.kāmānām ātmānam itarau ca pīḍayati

hindi: “अर्थ ही प्रधान,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
notes: Verbless clause. The '-' joins are the e-text's unsandhied joins (arthaḥ eva, pradhānaḥ iti). Kautilya names himself, as elsewhere in the text. artha here is wealth in the sense of the triad of the previous units.

hindi: क्योंकि धर्म और काम अर्थ-मूल वाले।
english: For dharma and desire [are] rooted in wealth.
notes: Verbless clause. The iti closes this statement of reasoning (it follows the quotation of the previous unit, which is attributed to Kautilya); it has no opening mark in the unit and is not rendered, per the glossary rule for a bare closing iti.

words.gram: n. abl. pl., final member of tat-puruṣa

words.gloss: by the goad of shadow and nālikā

words.gram: pres. part. m. acc. sg. pra-√mad

hindi: मर्यादा स्थापित करे, आचार्यों या अमात्यों को, जो इसे विनाश के स्थानों से रोकें, या एकान्त में छाया और नालिका के प्रतोद से प्रमाद करते हुए को कोंचें।
english: [He] should establish a limit, teachers or ministers, who would restrain him from places of ruin, or [who] would goad [him], being negligent, in private with the goad of shadow and nālikā.

text_flags.why: missing compound dot / stray space: apāya-sthāna is one compound

notes: The subject of sthāpayet is unstated. The accusatives ācāryān amātyān vā stand beside maryādām: either the teachers or ministers are themselves the 'limit' (a check on the king), or they are set up as holders of the limit; the translation keeps them side by side. Printed 'apāya sthānebhyo' has a space; apāya-sthāna is read as one compound (glossary 7.7 apāya-sthāna = place of ruin). chāyā-nālikā-pratoda is obscure: literally a goad of shadow and nālikā (nālikā = tube, also a measure of time); the alternative sense is a goad of reminders of time told by shadow and water-clock. Kept literal, low confidence. pramādyantam agrees with the unstated enam. The relative ye applies to both restraining and goading. ya-enam is ye enam (e-text '-' join).
lines_deva: मर्यादां स्थापयेद् आचार्यान् अमात्यान् वा, य-एनम् अपाय स्थानेभ्यो वारयेयुः, छाया.नालिका.प्रतोदेन वा रहसि प्रमाद्यन्तम् अभितुदेयुः
lines_iast: maryādāṃ sthāpayed ācāryān amātyān vā, ya-enam apāya sthānebhyo vārayeyuḥ, chāyā.nālikā.pratodena vā rahasi pramādyantam abhitudeyuḥ

hindi: राजत्व सहायकों से साध्य। एक पहिया नहीं चलता। इसलिए सचिवों को बनाए और उनके मत को सुने।
english: Kingship [is] to be accomplished with helpers. One wheel does not turn. Therefore [he] should make ministers and hear their opinion.
notes: Verse (two half-lines). The first clause is verbless. The subject of kurvīta and śṛṇuyāt is unstated. saciva = companion, minister (rendered 'minister' like amātya; the Sanskrit words differ); 'make ministers' is literal, i.e. appoint them. cakram ekam could also be read 'a wheel [is] one', but 'one wheel does not turn' is the natural sense.
lines_deva: सहाय.साध्यं राजत्वं चक्रम् एकं न वर्तते
कुर्वीत सचिवांस् तस्मात् तेषां च शृणुयान् मतम्
lines_iast: sahāya.sādhyaṃ rājatvaṃ cakram ekaṃ na vartate
kurvīta sacivāṃs tasmāt teṣāṃ ca śṛṇuyān matam
